The current metric definition lists exactly separation, symmetry, and the triangle inequality; nonnegativity is a consequence rather than an axiom. Removed only the extra word from step 1.1 and its contract mirror. Coordinatewise completeness, closure of the finite product ball, invariance, contraction with 0<=q<1, and the residual rearrangement all check directly, so the attribution defect is nonfatal. The Statement is unchanged.

The existing Taylor argument proves local defect O(h^3), and its rational stability function and nonnegative half-plane polynomial prove scalar L-stability correctly. The title additionally claims exact order two without a sharpness witness. Added proof step 3.1: for y'=t^2 from (0,0), the method gives h^3/(2 sqrt(2)), while the exact endpoint is h^3/3. The nonzero cubic defect rules out order three or higher. This closes a nonfatal omitted sharpness argument without changing the Statement or any dependencies.

The cited resolvent theorem requires continuity on the full state space as well as dissipativity. Restored continuity in F1 and checked it in step 1.1 for the polynomial f(x)=-x^3. Dissipativity follows from -(x-y)^2((x+y/2)^2+3y^2/4)<=0. The residual G(z)=z-1+z^3 is C1 on R; G(0)=-1 misses tolerance 0.1, so the finite solver correctly returns budget exhaustion at zero corrections despite the unique root. The omitted restatement hypothesis is nonfatal because the given field satisfies it.

At y_0=0 every trapezoidal iterate is zero, contradicting the original unqualified sign-alternation claim. Step 1.1 now states sign alternation for y_0!=0 and the zero orbit separately. The multiplier -49/51, magnitude ratio 49/51, BE factor 1/101, and SDIRK/Radau factors remain correct. This repairs the false universal orbit claim without excluding zero initial data or changing any Statement or Definition.
